topSignals.title: Project Jupiter's "trial by ambush" timeline takes effect today - NM Supreme Court still silent on both emergency stays
topSignals.text: August 24 is the exact date NMED released the full administrative record to opponents while simultaneously requiring their technical testimony, the compressed schedule New Energy Economy's August 19 emergency petition called "trial by ambush" in asking the NM Supreme Court to halt the September 14 air-quality-permit hearing. As of today's search, the Court has not ruled on either that petition or the Center for Biological Diversity's August 20 water-well challenge - meaning the process opponents sought to freeze is now proceeding exactly as scheduled, absent last-minute court intervention. Source NM | Searchlight NM | KFOX

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy extends its slide into a third week, now ~48% off the August 12 record with no fresh catalyst
topSignals.text: BE fell as much as 6% Monday morning to around $203, roughly 13 sessions removed from its ~$391 record close. Today's coverage attributes the move to the same overhangs already tracked in this digest (post-earnings valuation reset from ~81x forward earnings, unresolved scandium-sourcing short-seller/class-action overhang) rather than any new development. Yahoo Finance / 24/7 Wall St

topSignals.title: FuelCell Energy and Ceres Power both firm up the same morning, underscoring the weakness is Bloom-specific, not sector-wide
topSignals.text: FCEL rose 6% to ~$19.63 and Ceres Power (CWR.L) traded up roughly 8% intraday to ~439p (from Friday's 407p close). Neither move is tied to a specific news catalyst in today's coverage, extending the FCEL/Bloom divergence first flagged August 21. Yahoo Finance / 24/7 Wall St | Yahoo UK Finance

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet day August 24. Direct check of Elcogen's news archive confirms no releases since June 30 (China-EU clean energy collaboration recognition at the Chengdu forum). Status unchanged: E3000 G2 platform (>75% FC electrical efficiency, 90% with heat recovery, 650°C) in volume production at ELCO I Tallinn (360 MW/yr); no news since the June Ribera factory visit and April JNK India MoU. Elcogen newsroom

Topsoe (priority): Quiet day August 24 on SOFC/SOEC specifically. Status unchanged: Herning SOEC factory hibernated, commercialization pursued via licensing deals only (First Ammonia, August 11; Sasol/Allied Biofuels methanol synthesis, August 19). SOFC data-center pathway remains deferred to 2029+. Topsoe.com

Other players: Quiet Monday. No new dated announcements from Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, or Sunfire beyond the stock moves already covered under Market & Financials.

Project Jupiter (Oracle/OpenAI, NM, 2.45 GW Bloom SOFC): See Top Signal #1. Both NM Supreme Court petitions remain undecided; the September 14 NMED hearing status stays contingent on the Court's response.
Other pipeline items (Crusoe/Cheyenne, Hedgehog Texas, Nebius/Bloom NJ, Equinix, FCEL/Fit Energy, PowerCell/ECL Santa Clara): no updates today; status unchanged from August 23.

Rubicon Professional Services crosses 1 GW of installed battery storage capacity (announced August 18, first mention in this digest) - a scale marker for battery storage's growing footprint around data centers generally, though the announcement is not hyperscaler-specific and carries no single-project detail. EE Journal

No dated updates today on the Rolls-Royce SMR GDA (DAC still pending, Q4 2026/Q1 2027 estimate unchanged), the Blue Energy/GE Vernova Hitachi Texas gas-plus-nuclear project (agreement announced August 13, already tracked), other hyperscaler nuclear deals (Meta/TerraPower, Meta/Oklo, Amazon/Talen), or Energy Vault's 1.25 GW Texas platform (covered August 23).
Bloom Energy (BE): See Top Signal #2. Scandium class-action lead-plaintiff deadline unchanged (September 28). 10-Q with MW-shipped/ASP detail due September 11.

FuelCell Energy (FCEL) / Ceres Power (CWR.L): See Top Signal #3. FCEL's Zacks Rank #2 upgrade and Ceres' Goldman Sachs Conviction Buy (168% upside), both logged August 23, remain the standing bullish theses behind today's moves; no new dated catalyst identified for either.
